rows.question: When does my maternity leave start if my due date is 15 November 2026?
rows.reply:
Under the Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) rules, your employer may not employ you in the last six weeks before the birth, "in den letzten sechs Wochen vor der Entbindung" (MuSchG §3(1)). This is the protection period before the birth.

The start is counted from the expected date of birth shown in the certificate from your doctor or midwife ("Zeugnis einer Hebamme oder eines Entbindungspflegers"). Six weeks before an expected date of 15 November 2026 is 4 October 2026. The date in that certificate is what counts, so check it matches.

Some conditions are attached to this period:
- You may keep working during these six weeks if you expressly say you are willing to. You can withdraw that at any time for the future.
- If the baby is not born on the expected day, the period before the birth becomes shorter or longer to match.

After the birth, your employer may not employ you until eight weeks have passed. This extends to twelve weeks in three cases: 1. premature births, 2. multiple births, and 3. if a doctor finds a disability in the child (as defined in SGB IX §2(1) sentence 1) within eight weeks of the birth. The third case applies only if you apply for it. If the baby comes early, the period after the birth also gets longer by the time lost before the birth. The twelve-week extension does not apply to a stillbirth.

The Mutterschutz law does not cover self-employed women. They have to arrange their own cover for the time before and after the birth.

rows.question: How long after birth can we apply for Elterngeld without losing money?
rows.reply:
The law sets no application deadline. What it limits is how far back Elterngeld (parental allowance) is paid.

BEEG §7(1) says Elterngeld must be applied for in writing and is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month of life in which the application is received: "rückwirkend nur für die letzten drei Lebensmonate vor Beginn des Lebensmonats geleistet, in dem der Antrag auf Elterngeld eingegangen ist". Any earlier months are not paid.

These are the child's months of life, not calendar months. BEEG §4(2) says Elterngeld is paid in monthly amounts "für Lebensmonate des Kindes". BEEG §4(1) says it can be received from the day of birth ("ab dem Tag der Geburt").

So the three months before the month of life in which your application arrives are still covered. If the application arrives later than the child's fourth month of life, the first months of life fall outside that window and are lost. An application received during the child's first three months of life loses nothing under this rule.

The same three-month limit applies to later changes. Under BEEG §7(2), decisions made in the application can be changed until the end of the payment period. A change can apply retroactively only for the last three months of life before the month in which the change request is received.

Whether you are entitled, and for which months, is decided by your local Elterngeld office.

rows.question: How much notice do I have to give my employer for Elternzeit?
rows.reply:
The notice period for Elternzeit (parental leave (unpaid job-protected leave)) depends on when in the child's life the leave falls. Under BEEG §16(1), you must request it from your employer in text form at the latest:

1. Seven weeks before it begins, for leave up to the child's third birthday ("spätestens sieben Wochen").
2. Thirteen weeks before it begins, for leave between the third birthday and the end of the child's eighth year ("spätestens 13 Wochen").

What must go with the request: if you request leave for the period up to the third birthday, you must also state at the same time which periods within two years you will take Elternzeit ("für welche Zeiten innerhalb von zwei Jahren").

What counts as text form: the Familienportal explains that the request can be made, for example, by a letter without a signature or by email.

Shorter notice: where there are urgent reasons, a reasonable shorter period is possible by way of exception ("Bei dringenden Gründen ist ausnahmsweise eine angemessene kürzere Frist möglich"). The Familienportal gives premature births, or an adoptive placement that could not be planned in time, as examples. It says the period that applies then depends on the circumstances of the individual case.

Mothers taking leave straight after maternity protection: the maternity protection period after the birth counts towards the two-year period. If a mother could not request leave starting immediately after the maternity protection period in time, for a reason she is not responsible for, she can make the request within one week after that reason ends (§16(2)).

After you request it: your employer must certify your Elternzeit to you (§16(1)).

Dismissal protection: protection against dismissal starts from the point at which Elternzeit has been requested. It starts at the earliest eight weeks before leave up to the third birthday begins, and at the earliest 14 weeks before leave between the third and eighth birthdays begins (§18(1)).

Part-time work during the leave: a claim to reduced hours during Elternzeit must also be notified in text form. The period is seven weeks for the time up to the third birthday and 13 weeks for the time between the third birthday and the end of the eighth year, counted before the part-time work begins (§15(7) no. 5).

rows.question: How long is maternity protection after the birth if the baby comes early?
rows.reply:
Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) after the birth normally lasts eight weeks. The statute says the employer may not employ a woman "bis zum Ablauf von acht Wochen nach der Entbindung" (until eight weeks after the birth have passed).

The period after the birth is extended to twelve weeks in three cases (MuSchG §3(2)):
1. "bei Frühgeburten": for premature births.
2. "bei Mehrlingsgeburten": for multiple births.
3. If a disability in the child is medically determined before eight weeks after the birth have passed. This third extension applies only if the mother applies for it ("nur, wenn die Frau dies beantragt"). The Familienportal says this application is made to the health insurance fund (Krankenkasse).

A baby born before the expected date gets a further extension. The six-week period before the birth is counted from the expected date of delivery, and it is shortened if the baby comes earlier. The statute then says: "Bei vorzeitiger Entbindung verlängert sich die Schutzfrist nach der Entbindung ... um den Zeitraum der Verkürzung der Schutzfrist vor der Entbindung." This means the days lost before the birth are added after it, on top of the eight or twelve weeks.

The federal Familienportal explains the two situations this way:
- If the baby is born early but does not count medically as a premature birth, the period after the birth ends a few days later than eight weeks. It ends as many days later as the baby arrived early, so the total stays 14 weeks.
- If the baby counts medically as a premature birth, the period after the birth is 12 weeks, and the total rises from 14 to 18 weeks. The portal gives a birth weight under 2,500 grams as one example. This example comes from the guidance page, not from the statute excerpt.

The extension to twelve weeks does not apply after a stillbirth ("Satz 2 gilt nicht bei einer Totgeburt").

After the birth, the employer may not let you work during this period, even if you want to. The exceptions are for pupils and students in training who expressly ask to resume, and the separate rules after the death of a child. If your employer demands that you work during the protection period, the Familienportal says you can turn to your supervisory authority (Aufsichtsbehörde).

rows.question: Can my employer dismiss me while I am pregnant?
rows.reply:
In general, no. Under MuSchG §17(1), dismissal of a woman by her employer is not permitted ("Die Kündigung gegenüber einer Frau ist unzulässig"):
1. during her pregnancy,
2. until four months after a miscarriage after the twelfth week of pregnancy, and
3. until the end of her protection period after childbirth, and at least until four months after childbirth.

When this applies. This Kündigungsschutz (protection against dismissal) applies if the employer knows about the pregnancy, the miscarriage or the birth at the time of dismissal. It also applies if the employer is told within two weeks after receiving the dismissal ("innerhalb von zwei Wochen nach Zugang der Kündigung"). Missing the two weeks does no harm if the delay was for a reason the woman is not responsible for and she informs the employer without delay. The same applies to steps the employer takes to prepare a dismissal. According to the Familienportal, the protection applies even if you did not yet know about the pregnancy, but you must already have been pregnant when you received the dismissal.

The exception. The highest state authority responsible for occupational safety, or a body it designates, can exceptionally declare a dismissal permissible in special cases that are not connected with the pregnancy, a miscarriage or the birth (MuSchG §17(2)). The dismissal must then be in writing and must state the reason. The Familienportal gives these examples of such special reasons: the company is insolvent, part of the business is closed, in a small business the business cannot continue without a qualified replacement, or a particularly serious breach of duty. It says the employer must apply in writing to the supervisory authority, and that without the authority's approval the dismissal is invalid ("unwirksam").

If you are dismissed without approval. The Familienportal says you must bring an action before the competent labour court, "normalerweise innerhalb von 3 Wochen" from receiving the written dismissal. If you do not bring an action, the dismissal is treated as legally effective. You can bring it yourself, through a representative such as a lawyer, or orally at the court's registry. It also says you should involve the competent supervisory authority.

If you are dismissed with approval. You can challenge the approval itself; depending on the Bundesland this is done by objection or by court action. This is a separate procedure and does not replace the action before the labour court.

After the birth. If you take parental leave, the protection can be extended: under BEEG §18 the employer may not dismiss from the time parental leave is requested (at the earliest eight weeks before parental leave before the child's third birthday, and at the earliest 14 weeks before parental leave between the third birthday and the eighth birthday) and during parental leave, except in special cases declared permissible by the same type of state authority.

The excerpts do not name the specific office in Hessen. Whether a particular dismissal is valid is decided by the labour court, and approval of an exceptional dismissal by the state authority responsible for occupational safety.

rows.question: Is there an income limit above which we get no Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. Under BEEG §1(8), the right to Elterngeld (parental allowance) lapses ("Ein Anspruch entfällt") if the entitled person's zu versteuerndes Einkommen (taxable income) in the last completed tax assessment period before the birth was "mehr als 175 000 Euro".

For couples, the incomes are added together. If another person also meets the conditions in §1(1) sentence 1 no. 2 (living in the same household as the child) or in §1(3) or §1(4), the right lapses when "die Summe des zu versteuernden Einkommens beider Personen mehr als 175 000 Euro beträgt". For a single parent, only that parent's own income counts.

The limit is on taxable income, not gross income. The Familienportal explains that taxable income is usually much lower than gross pay. Special expenses (Sonderausgaben), provision expenses, individual allowances and extraordinary burdens are deducted to reach it. The Finanzamt determines taxable income, and the figure appears in your tax assessment (Steuerbescheid). As an illustration only, the same page gives about 207,000 euros gross for a married couple without children who are both employed and have a taxable income of 175,000 euros.

The limit has changed over time. The Familienportal states that it was 200,000 euros for couples and single parents for births from 1 April 2024. For births from 1 September 2021 to 31 March 2024, it was 300,000 euros for couples and 250,000 euros for single parents. The statutory transitional provision for earlier births is not among the excerpts I have. Which limit applies to a particular birth is decided by the Elterngeld office responsible for your district.

On the application: the Familienportal says to attach the tax assessment for the calendar year before the birth, if you have it. If you do not have it yet, BEEG §8 still allows a decision. Where the tax assessment is not available and the application indicates the §1(8) amounts will probably not be exceeded, Elterngeld is paid "unter dem Vorbehalt des Widerrufs" (subject to revocation) in case they are exceeded. Where it cannot yet be said whether the amounts are exceeded, the amount is decided provisionally ("vorläufig") until proof is provided.

Whether your household is above or below the limit is not something I can assess. Only the Elterngeld office responsible for your district decides that.

rows.question: How many months of Elterngeld can we get in total?
rows.reply:
The law sets the total in months of the standard variant, and lets you trade those months for the Plus variant. It does not give one fixed number for every family.

Standard months, shared by both parents:
- Together the parents have 12 monthly amounts: "Die Eltern haben gemeinsam Anspruch auf zwölf Monatsbeträge Basiselterngeld" (BEEG §4(3)).
- They get 2 further months, the "Partnermonate" (partner months), if one parent's earned income is reduced in two months of the child's life. That makes 14.
- One parent can take at most 12 standard months (§4(4)).
- A parent who takes Elterngeld (parental allowance) must take it for at least 2 months.

Trading for the Plus variant: instead of one standard month, a parent can take two months of "Elterngeld Plus" (§4(3)).

Partnership bonus: on top of the standard months, each parent can receive at most 4 monthly amounts of "Partnerschaftsbonus" (§4(4)). The official family portal describes these as extra Plus months when both parents work part-time at the same time. It says single parents can also receive them.

Premature births: the shared total rises if the child is born early, measured from the expected delivery date on the doctor's or midwife's certificate (§4(5)):
1. at least 6 weeks early: 13 standard months
2. at least 8 weeks early: 14
3. at least 12 weeks early: 15
4. at least 16 weeks early: 16
In these cases one parent can take up to the same number (13, 14, 15 or 16) plus up to 4 bonus months. The standard variant can then be drawn until the end of the 15th, 16th, 17th or 18th month of life.

Time limits on when months can be used (§4(1)):
- Payment is for months of the child's life, starting from the birth, not calendar months.
- The standard variant can be drawn until the child completes the 14th month of life.
- The Plus variant can be drawn until the end of the 32nd month of life. From the 15th month on, at least one parent must take it in consecutive months. The portal adds that once there is a month after the 14th in which neither parent receives it, none can be received afterwards, even with months left over.
- For adopted children, Elterngeld can be drawn from when the child joins the household, at most until the child's 8th birthday.

Months that count as used:
- A mother's months with maternity benefits count as standard months, whether or not she applies for them (§4(4)).
- Both parents can draw the standard variant at the same time in only one of the first 12 months (§4(6)). The portal says such a month uses up 2 standard months.
- Exceptions apply for multiple births, premature births as above, and children with a disability.

How many months your family receives is decided by the Elterngeld office for your district, not by this service.

rows.question: What is the Partnerschaftsbonus and who qualifies?
rows.reply:
The Partnerschaftsbonus (partnership bonus months) is set out in BEEG §4b. If both parents work "nicht weniger als 24 und nicht mehr als 32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats" (at least 24 and at most 32 hours a week, averaged over the child's month of life) and both meet the conditions of §1, each parent gets an additional monthly amount of "Elterngeld Plus" for that month (§4b(1)).

The statute attaches these conditions:
- Each parent can receive at most four bonus months, and only if they take it for at least two months of life (§4b(2)).
- Both parents must take it at the same time and in consecutive months of life (§4b(3)).
- If the conditions for sole receipt under §4c(1) no. 1 to 3 arise during the bonus, one parent can continue it alone under §4c(2) (§4b(4)).
- The consecutive-months requirement still counts as met if it later turns out the conditions were not met in every month applied for (§4b(5)).

One parent can also take the bonus alone if one of the three grounds in §4c(1) applies:
1. that parent meets the conditions for the single-parent tax relief under §24b(1) and (3) of the Income Tax Act, and the other parent lives neither with them nor with the child;
2. care by the other parent would endanger the child's welfare within the meaning of §1666(1) and (2) of the Civil Code; or
3. care by the other parent is impossible, in particular because of serious illness or severe disability. Economic reasons and being busy with other activities do not count.
That parent must work 24 to 32 hours a week on average in at least two and at most four consecutive months of life (§4c(2)).

Overall, one parent can receive at most 12 monthly amounts of basic Elterngeld plus up to four bonus months (§4(4)).

The federal family portal adds, in plain language: the bonus is calculated the same way as ElterngeldPlus and, depending on income before the birth, comes to between 150 and 900 euros per parent per month (the excerpts do not give the date this figure was checked). It can be used before, between or after the other Elterngeld months, and also if you otherwise receive only basic Elterngeld. Separated parents can also receive it. If your average hours differ from what you planned, you must report this to your Elterngeldstelle. For a month in which the hours fall outside 24 to 32, the bonus for that month must be repaid, and both parents lose it for that month even if only one fails the condition. The other months are not affected if the conditions were met in at least two months.

For earlier periods: under §27(3), where the bonus was received wholly or partly before 23 September 2022 and the conditions could not be met because of the COVID-19 pandemic, the income and working hours stated when applying apply. The portal also says its explanations cover children born after August 2021; for children born before 1 September 2021 partly different rules apply, and it directs those parents to their Elterngeldstelle.

Whether a particular family qualifies, and how much they receive, is decided by the Elterngeldstelle responsible for them.

rows.question: We forgot to apply for Kindergeld. How far back will they pay?
rows.reply:
Kindergeld (child benefit) is paid retroactively for at most six months. The law says payment of Kindergeld that has been set "erfolgt rückwirkend nur für die letzten sechs Monate vor Beginn des Monats, in dem der Antrag auf Kindergeld eingegangen ist". In plain terms, back payment covers only the six months before the month in which your application is received. Months further back are not paid out.

The same provision adds that the entitlement itself is not affected by this limit on payment: "Der Anspruch auf Kindergeld nach § 62 bleibt von dieser Auszahlungsbeschränkung unberührt." The six-month limit restricts what is paid out. It does not remove the underlying entitlement.

The official family portal says back payment applies where Kindergeld was due to you but not paid, for example because no application was made. To claim it, state in the application that you are applying retroactively and from which date you want Kindergeld.

Kindergeld must be applied for in writing or electronically. The application goes to the Familienkasse at your Agentur für Arbeit. The Familienkasse sets Kindergeld by formal decision and decides which months are paid in your case. For questions about applying, the Bundesagentur für Arbeit has a free service line on 0800 4 555530.

rows.question: How much Kindergeld do we get per month for our first child?
rows.reply:
The statute sets one monthly amount for every child, so the first child gets the same as any other: "Das Kindergeld beträgt monatlich für jedes Kind 259 Euro", which means Kindergeld (child benefit) is 259 euros a month for each child. The income tax law (EStG §66) and the federal child benefit law (BKGG §6) state the same figure. The date this figure was checked is shown with each citation.

Kindergeld is paid monthly. It starts with the month in which the conditions are met and ends with the month in which they stop being met. Under the official guidance, a child born on 25 May brings the full Kindergeld for May.

The law raises the amount if the tax allowances for children are raised, rounded to full euros. Separately, each year the tax office checks automatically, as part of the income tax assessment, whether the tax allowances for children or the Kindergeld paid are more favourable for the parents. You do not need to apply for this check.

Whether you are entitled is decided by the authority, not here. The official guidance names the Familienkasse as the office handling Kindergeld, and it states that the application can be made online with the Bundesagentur für Arbeit.
